summary: Sertaconazole nitrate (Ertaczo) is a topical azole antifungal cream, 2%, indicated for the treatment of interdigital tinea pedis in immunocompetent patients 12 years of age and older. It is applied twice daily for 4 weeks to the affected areas between the toes and the immediately surrounding healthy skin. Systemic absorption is negligible (plasma levels below the limit of quantitation). It is for topical use only and may cause local reactions such as contact dermatitis, dry skin, and burning.
indications: Topical treatment of interdigital tinea pedis in immunocompetent adult and pediatric patients 12 years of age and older caused by Trichophyton rubrum, Trichophyton mentagrophytes, and Epidermophyton floccosum

dosage.c: Interdigital tinea pedis (patients 12 years and older)
dosage.d: Apply a sufficient amount of cream, 2%, to cover both the affected areas between the toes and the immediately surrounding healthy skin
dosage.n: Use for the full treatment time even if symptoms improve; dry the area thoroughly before application after bathing; wash hands after use; avoid occlusive dressings

admin: For topical use only; not for ophthalmic, oral, or intravaginal use
Apply a sufficient amount to cover the affected areas between the toes and the immediately surrounding healthy skin
Dry the affected area(s) thoroughly before application, if applying after bathing
Avoid the use of occlusive dressings or wrappings
Continue for the full 4-week treatment course even if symptoms improve
moa: Sertaconazole is an azole antifungal that inhibits fungal cytochrome P-450-mediated 14-alpha-lanosterol demethylase, the enzyme that converts lanosterol to ergosterol. Ergosterol is a key component of fungal cell membranes; its depletion leads to fungal cell injury through leakage of key cytoplasmic constituents.

relative: Known sensitivity to azole antifungals (cross-reactivity may occur)
monitor: Local skin irritation - discontinue treatment and institute appropriate therapy if irritation develops

preg: Risk Summary: There are no available data on Ertaczo cream, 2%, use in pregnant women to evaluate a drug-associated risk of major birth defects, miscarriage, or adverse maternal or fetal outcomes. In oral animal reproduction studies, no adverse developmental effects were observed in rats and rabbits at doses 40 and 80 times the maximum recommended human dose (MRHD) during organogenesis; in rats, continued maternal dosing until weaning produced reduced live birth indices and increased stillbirths at doses 20 and 40 times the MRHD. The U.S. background risk of major birth defects and miscarriage is 2-4% and 15-20%, respectively.
lact: Risk Summary: There are no data on the presence of sertaconazole in human or animal milk, its effects on the breastfed infant, or its effects on milk production. The developmental and health benefits of breastfeeding should be considered along with the mother's clinical need for the drug and any potential adverse effects on the breastfed infant.
renal: Not applicable (topical). The label provides no renal-impairment dosing; systemic absorption is negligible.
hepatic: Not applicable (topical). The label provides no hepatic-impairment dosing; systemic absorption is negligible.

serious: Severe cutaneous adverse reactions (reported infrequently in clinical trials)

counsel: Use this cream exactly as directed; it is for external (topical) use only - not for the eyes, mouth, or vagina
Apply to the affected areas between the toes and the surrounding healthy skin twice daily
Complete the full 4-week course even if your symptoms improve
Dry the area thoroughly before applying after bathing and wash your hands after use
Do not cover the treated area with occlusive dressings or wrappings
Stop use and contact your clinician if skin irritation, redness, or a rash develops
pk: Negligible systemic exposure; plasma concentrations below the limit of quantitation (2.5 ng/mL)
Applied twice daily for a 4-week course
Store at 20-25 degrees C (68-77 degrees F); excursions permitted to 15-30 degrees C (59-86 degrees F)
pearls: An imidazole antifungal that blocks ergosterol synthesis, leading to fungal cell death
Systemic absorption is negligible - plasma levels were below the 2.5 ng/mL limit of quantitation after multiple-dose topical use
Indicated only for interdigital tinea pedis in immunocompetent patients aged 12 and older
Use caution in patients sensitive to other azole antifungals because cross-reactivity may occur
Avoid occlusive dressings and complete the full 4-week course to reduce relapse
missed: If a dose is missed, apply it as soon as remembered. If it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed dose and resume the regular twice-daily schedule. Do not apply a double amount to make up for a missed dose. Complete the full 4-week treatment course even if symptoms have improved.
overdose: No information on overdosage is provided in the labeling. Sertaconazole cream is for topical use only with negligible systemic absorption, so systemic overdose is unlikely with topical application. If irritation occurs, discontinue use and institute appropriate therapy. In case of accidental ingestion or other concern, contact Poison Help (1-800-222-1222).
